problem: Pooling heterogeneous multi-robot navigation data is hard because a robot cannot execute every recorded behavior (e.g. a rover cannot climb stairs), and end-to-end foundation models (NoMaD, NaVILA) are brittle and conflate semantic planning with embodiment-specific capability.
motivation: General-purpose navigation needs to generalize across environments and embodiments and be steerable at test time. Scaling data increases heterogeneity, so high-level planning (goal reaching, obstacle avoidance) should be separated from low-level traversability, which depends on the robot's physical capabilities.
key_idea: Fine-tune a VLM to propose candidate 2D pixel-space paths from heterogeneous real-world data, then re-rank them with a lightweight per-embodiment affordance model trained in simulation.
insight: Using 2D paths as the interface lets one planner absorb data from different embodiments, and it keeps the VLM's pretrained generalization. The affordance model then grounds the plan in embodiment capability. Ablations: swapping only the affordance model lets Hound (wheeled) rise from 60% to 90% SR (choosing ramps over stairs) while Spot stays at 100%. Modulation also raises single-robot OOD success from 20% to 60% by filtering paths through obstacles. Offline, pooled data beats single-dataset training on path error.
method: High-level VLM planner: PaliGemma 2 3B (224px) fine-tuned with LoRA to map an image plus a text-encoded goal (loc tokens) to 5 waypoints as a 2D pixel path.

Data recipe: 29.8 h from SCAND, CODa, TartanDrive 2 and a small Spot set. Hindsight labels come from ground-projected poses, short and long horizons are mixed 50/50, curvature filtering is applied, and the dataset mix is tuned empirically.

Steerability: 10% of data is augmented with GPT-5-mini annotations (noisy and mirrored paths ranked with chain-of-thought, top 3 paths plus descriptions), and co-training on COCO-QA and Localized Narratives prevents forgetting. Natural-language preferences are appended to the goal string.

Affordance model: an MLP F_pi(elevation map, x, y, heading) predicts traversal probability, trained with BCE on Isaac Lab rollouts over procedural terrains (wave function collapse, cellular automata). It is trained separately for each embodiment.
Path re-ranking: K sampled VLM paths are projected to the ground plane, each is scored by the minimum affordance along it, and one is chosen by argmax or softmax sampling.

Deployment: receding horizon that executes the first m (3–4) of 5 waypoints, rotates in place when the goal is out of view, uses a 20 s timeout, and runs the VLM at about 1 Hz on a laptop RTX 3080 with the affordance model on a Jetson.

setting.backbone: PaliGemma 2 3B (LoRA fine-tuned) planner + MLP affordance model (trained from scratch in sim)
setting.training_data: 514K samples / 29.8 h real-world navigation data (SCAND, CODa, TartanDrive 2, Spot) plus VLM-annotated steering data, COCO-QA and Localized Narratives co-training; affordance model on 1000 simulated terrains
setting.observation: monocular RGB plus a local elevation map (LiDAR/depth) for the affordance model; goal given as GPS/3D coordinates
setting.action_space: predicted 2D pixel paths (5 waypoints) tracked by a low-level locomotion controller (Spot built-in or a pure-pursuit controller on Hound)
setting.simulator: Isaac Lab (affordance training only); evaluation is real world
setting.privileged: none (elevation map built from onboard LiDAR/depth; odometry/GPS goals)

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 courses (Hallway, Atrium, Lab, Campus, Forest, Down Ramp) x 5 trials

numbers.backbone: PaliGemma 2 3B fine-tuned further on 2K human-sketch samples + Hound affordance model
numbers.extra: extra finetune on the stairs/ramp scene for multimodality
numbers.evidence: Table 2/3: With Modulation Hound SR 90%, Spot 100%; No Modulation Hound 60%
Table 4: With Modulation 60.0% vs No Modulation 20.0%

numbers_note: Real-world experiments only, with small trial counts (5–10). Baseline numbers are omitted per the rules. Pooling ablation results are given only in figures.
results: VAMOS reaches 90% average SR across 6 real indoor and outdoor courses, versus 67% for ViPlanner, 53% for the modular stack, 27% for NoMaD and 10% for NaVILA. On the cross-embodiment stairs/ramp task it gets 90% on Hound versus 0% for ViPlanner, and affordance modulation raises Hound from 60% to 90% and single-robot OOD success from 20% to 60%.
limitations: Real-world evaluation uses very few trials (5–10 per setting) on short- to medium-range goals, and the cross-embodiment test needed extra fine-tuning on hand-drawn paths.
The VLM handles dynamic obstacles poorly and sometimes overshoots or undershoots turns; the Spot affordance model uses a surrogate RL policy rather than the real controller.
Non-robot data (CoTracker videos, iPhone ARKit) hurt performance, and the data mix was chosen heuristically.
